correctness.rationale: For finite connected undirected graphs with strictly positive bidirectional rates, the killed generator on labeled noncollision configurations is L^Ex-diag(kappa). Constant kappa yields exact semigroup factorization and an independent exponential killing construction. Every labeled component projects onto the connected token graph of all k-subsets; equality of Doob and exclusion jump rates forces a constant Perron eigenfunction and hence constant kappa. One-horizon survival uniformity forces constant kappa by positivity of each component matrix exponential and Perron eigenvalue simplicity. Uniform k-subset sums of symmetric pair rates give uniform pair weights for 2<=k<=n-2, while k=n-1 reduces to equal weighted degrees. Exact verifier passed 117816 finite classification assertions; finitary checks are not treated as the infinite-n proof.

value.rationale: The motivating gap is when conditioning independent particles never to collide changes no dynamics at all, beyond a known change-of-measure identity. The theorem gives an exact structural answer for every finite connected bidirectional weighted graph at every nontrivial occupancy. It proves a sharp occupancy threshold: below one vacancy only uniformly pair-weighted complete graphs work, whereas with exactly one vacancy even sparse regular graphs and nonreversible cyclic walks work. This predicts when a conditioned system can be perfectly simulated by ordinary exclusion and an independent exponential clock, and gives an exact single-horizon survival diagnostic. The special cyclic case is acknowledged as consistent with earlier work.
